page.title: Changelog
page.description: Everything that's changed in Gachapon, from the very first capsule to the latest news.

v3_6.title: Passive Overhaul
v3_6.summary: Eight new passives built around the action gauge, targeting and control, and combat rebalanced from the ground up.

entries.e1: Eight new passives: Shackle and Momentum play with the action gauge, Taunt, Bodyguard and Hunter's Mark change who takes the hits, and Stun, Weaken and Sunder cripple the enemy. They replace Vampirism, Armor Piercer and Bloodlust.
entries.e2: Passives are rescaled by rarity: Poison, Sanctuary and Blessing no longer dominate, and the weakest passives get a boost. Vengeance marks the enemy that strikes your team, and Execution hits harder the more HP the target is missing.
entries.e3: Base stats now depend on the card's role (tanks really soak, mages hit hard), equipment % bonuses are doubled, and campaign difficulty ramps up without a sudden jump between chapters.
entries.e4: During a pull, the guarantee and boosts are shown and progress as each card is flipped.
entries.e5: In the equipment workshop, each row has its own Equip / Replace / Unequip button, a filter hides pieces worn by other cards, and every piece shows its set. Alchemy gets a comic-book transmutation animation.
entries.e6: Removing a member or leaving a team works again; power now includes set bonuses on every screen, as does team strength on the leaderboard; the replay no longer misses damage reflected by Riposte.

v3_5.title: Orders and Alchemy
v3_5.summary: Two new outlets for your duplicates, and equipment gets its own page.

entries.e1: Orders: customers ask for cards — deliver your duplicates for gold, dust and tokens, up to four deliveries a day.
entries.e2: Alchemy: pour your duplicates into the cauldron to get a random card of the next rarity up.
entries.e3: A card's equipment now has its own page: pieces are ranked by gain, with a stat preview on hover. A button also swaps all equipment between two cards.
entries.e4: Upgrading a Common, Uncommon or Rare card costs up to four times less. The raid boss loses 30% HP, and its Epic card comes back from level 3.
entries.e5: The card shop now refreshes every hour and is called the Market.
entries.e6: The menu is grouped into four dropdowns (Collection, Combat, Commerce, Social) that open on hover, and the "Human Kingdom" set becomes "Humans".

v3_4.title: Gachapon speaks English
v3_4.summary: The game goes bilingual and opens up without an account.

entries.e1: The whole game is available in English: pick your language from the selector in the bar.
entries.e2: Guest mode: play without an account from the home page, then save your progress with email, Google or Discord. Teams, raids and bets stay account-only.
entries.e3: Every team has a public page, visible to non-members.
entries.e4: The leaderboard is paginated, shows the real number of ranked players and jumps straight to your position.
entries.e5: Cards level up past 60 again, the level-up celebration also fires outside pulls, and the raid attack quota is counted per team.

v3_3.title: The team boss moves up a notch
v3_3.summary: A raid that adapts to your team, rarer rare pulls and a tighter economy.

entries.e1: The raid boss is calibrated for at least ten members. Every week you kill it, it comes back with 10% more HP and rewards; otherwise it drops a level.
entries.e2: Epics and Legendaries are twice as rare. Pity doesn't change.
entries.e3: Energy packs cost three times more, and wish prices depend on the rarity you target.
entries.e4: Towers and campaign are recalibrated on real player profiles, equipment included.
entries.e5: A piece sells from its own sheet, and the list groups your pieces by set.
entries.e6: On mobile, the menu is no longer cut off; a wish can be removed from the card sheet; a cleared tower floor replays at the sweep price.

v3_2.title: Each mode keeps its own team
v3_2.summary: One team per tower, one for the campaign, one for the raid.

entries.e1: Campaign, towers and raid each have their own team. Until you edit it, a mode uses your campaign team.
entries.e2: The 120 tower monsters have a name and a face, drawn from their element's families.
entries.e3: The power leaderboard is computed from your campaign team.

v3_1.title: Replaying without losing your evening
v3_1.summary: Multi-battle, multi-card wishes, clearer equipment and a big balancing pass.

entries.e1: Multi-battle (×1 or ×5) replaces "Sweep", in the campaign and in towers.
entries.e2: Wishes hold up to five cards and the seven-day delay is gone; discounts no longer apply to them.
entries.e3: The rewards screen lays out equipment and cards on two rows, with "Continue" always in reach.
entries.e4: Equipment reads at a glance: each piece's set, set progress per card, whole-number stats.
entries.e5: "Precision" becomes "Vigilance" and activates at three pieces: Wrath (4) and Vigilance (3) finally fit on the same card.
entries.e6: Balancing: level curve ×5, skill tree at 109 points (exactly level 100), Collection branch buffed, no more % SPD on equipment.
entries.e7: Fixes: energy pack limit with "Opulence", missing won card at the end of battle, equipment grid reordering itself.

v3_0.title: Teams come to life
v3_0.summary: Weekly raid, duels, bets, team progression and recruitment.

entries.e1: Team raid: an elemental boss every week, two attacks per day per member, rewards at 25, 50, 75 and 100%.
entries.e2: Pull duels: challenge a teammate over five pulls, each stakes cards, the best score takes it all.
entries.e3: Bets: stake your dust on a teammate's next ten pulls, with odds computed from the real chances.
entries.e4: Team progression: raid, duels, bets and pulls level up the team, and the leader invests in four bonuses.
entries.e5: Recruitment: a directory of open teams, up to five applications at once.
entries.e6: Team screens redone, and the officer rank becomes assignable.

v2_1.title: Cards, skills and tuning
v2_1.summary: Five more families, a skill tree up to level 100 and recalibrated combat.

entries.e1: Centaurs, Dryads, Kitsune, Draenei and Lamia: 170 more cards, 602 in total.
entries.e2: The skill tree covers level 100, with two new equipment nodes.
entries.e3: Equipment quests join the weekly rotation.
entries.e4: An elements guide opens from the campaign and towers.
entries.e5: Speed no longer scales with level: equipment decides turn order.
entries.e6: The pity counter announced the Legendary one pull too early.

v2_0.title: The Towers and Equipment
v2_0.summary: Four elemental towers and seven equipment slots per card.

entries.e1: Four ten-floor towers, each tied to an equipment slot.
entries.e2: Seven pieces per card, one main stat and up to four substats, max level 12.
entries.e3: Seven sets of two to four pieces, counted per card.
entries.e4: The same piece can roll different main stats: there's a right version to chase.
entries.e5: The inventory sorts, filters and sells in bulk.
entries.e6: Campaign loot follows your progress: fewer Commons, more high rarities.

v1_9.title: Combat gets deeper
v1_9.summary: Crits, penetration, lifesteal and reactive passives.

entries.e1: Crit rate and damage, armor penetration and lifesteal, all from equipment.
entries.e2: Passives react to the battle: Vigor cancels a fatal hit, Fortification stacks, and more.
entries.e4: Healing shows up in the battle log.

v1_7.title: Nine chapters and palier 7
v1_7.summary: The campaign now stretches to chapter 9, your cards climb one palier further, and bosses go back to being a real end-of-chapter test.

entries.e1: Four new chapters: Volcano, Tundra, Abyss and Rift. The campaign now counts 9 chapters and 90 stages.
entries.e2: Palier 7 unlocked: your cards can now climb up to level 70.
entries.e3: Difficulty overhauled: enemy power now scales continuously from one end of the campaign to the other, and the boss goes back to being the real peak of each chapter — the true check on your build.
entries.e4: New achievements mark the milestones of chapters 5, 7 and 9, aligned with the level 70 cap.

v1_6.title: Elements & pulling
v1_6.summary: Your cards have an element, so do your opponents — and pulling becomes a real show.

entries.e1: Elements: every card and every monster belongs to an element. Fire burns nature, nature cracks earth, earth absorbs water, water douses fire — and light and dark answer each other. Attacking with the advantage hits hard; taking it hits less hard.
entries.e2: Elemental targeting: in battle, each unit prioritizes the opponent it dominates. Enemy elements are shown before you launch the assault — build your team accordingly.
entries.e3: Campaign recalibrated to account for elements, with element badges visible on portraits as well as on the opponent preview.
entries.e4: Pulling reimagined: the capsule vibrates in a crescendo then bursts open, the machine animates, the sound follows along. The x10 pull unstacks card by card, with a Skip button if you're in a hurry.
entries.e5: A six-step tutorial greets you on the pull page, and your energy fills up completely every time you level up.
entries.e6: Shop rebalanced (token packs, refills, daily shop), base token storage raised to 10, and resource display made consistent everywhere.

v1_5.title: Equipment, combat & campaign
v1_5.summary: Your equipment progresses, combat gains depth, and the campaign grows.

entries.e1: Equipment progression: upgrade your pieces up to level 12, substats based on rarity, and bulk destruction for gold.
entries.e2: Combat reimagined: every card acts according to its speed (action gauge), and attacks hit random targets.
entries.e3: Campaign enriched: chapters 4 and 5, enemies with portraits, and families with unique passives (poison, burn, blessing…).
entries.e4: Collection: power now shown on your cards, sort and filters remembered, and bulk recycling of duplicates.
entries.e5: Shop: energy packs for the campaign, and stackable pull boosts.
entries.e6: More spectacular reveals: dedicated animations for the Brilliant and Holo variants, and click-to-inspect on the card.

v1_4.title: Quests, wishes & economy
v1_4.summary: New daily objectives, a wishlist, and an economy overhauled from the ground up.

entries.e1: Daily and weekly quests with rewards to claim.
entries.e2: Wishlist: flag the cards you're after on your profile.
entries.e3: Public stats page to follow the community's activity.
entries.e4: Economy overhaul: tokens, dust and pity rebalanced.

v1_3.title: Combat & progression
v1_3.summary: PvE arrives: achievements, campaign, battles and equipment for your cards.

entries.e1: Achievement system: unlock rewards as you play.
entries.e4: Equipment to strengthen your cards in battle.

v1_2.title: Skills & leaderboards
v1_2.summary: Customize your playstyle and climb the leaderboards.

entries.e1: Skill tree to grow your player profile.
entries.e2: Daily shop with a selection that renews every day.
entries.e3: Leaderboards redesigned with a global score system.
entries.e4: Card reveal reworked with effects specific to each rarity.

v1_1.title: Profiles & rewards
v1_1.summary: Your personal showcase, and something to reward your consistency.

entries.e1: Public profile pages to show off your collection.
entries.e4: Permanent upgrades (token gain, luck, dust harvesting…).
entries.e5: Live feed of pulls from the whole community.

v1_0.title: The launch
v1_0.summary: The first version of Gachapon: play, collect, join a team.

entries.e1: 3D claw and capsule machines for your pulls.
entries.e2: TCG card collection with Holo and Brilliant variants.
entries.e3: Accounts via email or through Google and Discord.
entries.e4: Teams, invitations and leaderboards between members.
entries.e5: Admin backoffice to manage cards, sets and media.
